title: Abdominal Pain - OB/GYN
hpi_narrative: [Ms] X is a [age unknown]-year-old female with [PMH not specified] who presents with Abdominal Pain. [Onset: sudden, Character: severe, Severity: high, Associated symptoms: guarding, tenderness, decreasing hematocrit, tachycardia, hypotension, Symptomatology: severe pain, Pertinent negatives: none specified]. The clinical question this case forces you to answer is to diagnose the cause of the abdominal pain and order appropriate tests and treatments.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: Genitalia
stacks.finding: The genital area is part of the differential that could be causing abdominal pain, so it is worth examining.

stacks.label: Physical Exam: General Appearance
stacks.finding: The patient is having severe pain. It would be appropriate to generally look at the patient to help guide diagnosis.

stacks.label: CBC with differential
stacks.finding: It's important to check for blood loss as the patient is having symptoms of hemoperitoneum.

stacks.label: HCG, beta, urine, qualitative / HCG, beta, serum, qualitative / Beta HCG, serum, quantitative / HCG, total, serum, qualitative
stacks.finding: Evaluation of serum 8hCG-levels is necessary to differentiate ruptured ovarian cyst from a ruptured ectopic pregnancy, which may have a similar presentation.

stacks.label: Pulse oximetry
stacks.finding: Important to check on oxygenation because the patient has hemoperitoneum causing blood loss.

stacks.label: Electrocardiography, 12 lead / Electrocardiography, ambulatory / Electrocardiography, rhythm strip, long
stacks.finding: The patient is likely to have surgery, so getting a pre-surgery EKG is important

stacks.label: US, abdomen/pelvis, with contrast / US, pelvis, transabdominal / US, pelvis, transvaginal
Basic metabolic profile / Comprehensive metabolic profile / Liver function panel
stacks.finding: Chemistries are an important screening tool to reach a diagnosis.

stacks.label: Type and screen, blood / Type and Rh factor, blood
Intravenous access / Intravenous line, capped
stacks.finding: Although not required, it would be a good idea to make a habit to order an IV Access when you are administering IV fluids / medications.

stacks.label: Saline solution, normal / Lactated Ringer solution
stacks.finding: The patient is tachycardic and has a decreasing hematocrit and is actively bleeding. Fluids are necessary.

stacks.label: Transfusion, packed red blood cells
stacks.finding: The patient has a dropping hematocrit prior to surgery and is hypotensive and is symptomatic, so she requires a blood transfusion.

stacks.label: Hydromorphone hydrochloride / Fentanyl / Morphine sulfate / Ketorolac tromethamine
PT/PTT / Partial thromboplastin time AND PT/INR
stacks.type: © PT/PTT / Partial thromboplastin time AND PT/INR
stacks.finding: The patient will require surgery, so getting pre-surgery labs is important.

stacks.label: Cefazolin sodium / Cefoxitin sodium / Cefotetan / Cephalosporins
